name: Cirrus
description: Thin, wispy streaks way up high, made of tiny ice crystals. If you see these, weather might be changing in a day or two.

name: Cirrocumulus
description: Small white ripples or patches high in the sky, made of ice crystals. They usually don't stick around very long.

name: Cirrostratus
description: A thin sheet that can cover the whole sky. Look for a ring (halo) around the sun or moon shining through it.

name: Altocumulus
looksLike: A flock of sheep in the sky
description: White or gray patches and rolls in the middle of the sky. A very common cloud on a partly cloudy day.

name: Altostratus
description: A gray sheet covering the sky. The sun looks pale and blurry through it, like looking through frosted glass. Can bring light rain.

name: Nimbostratus
description: A thick, dark gray layer that blocks the sun completely. This is the cloud that brings steady rain or snow.

name: Cumulus
description: Puffy white clouds with flat bottoms and rounded tops. The classic sunny-day cloud.

name: Cumulonimbus
looksLike: A huge tower or mountain, flat on top like an anvil
description: The thunderstorm cloud! A giant tower that can bring thunder, lightning, hail, heavy rain, and even tornadoes. This is the one storm chasers watch closest.

name: Stratocumulus
looksLike: Lumpy gray patches with gaps of blue sky
description: Gray or white lumpy patches that cover a lot of the sky but usually leave some gaps of blue showing through.

name: Stratus
looksLike: A flat gray blanket, like fog in the sky
description: A flat, featureless gray layer covering the whole sky, like fog that never touched the ground. Can bring drizzle.
